# runtag

Wrap one child process. Persist pid and exit under XDG. Never write job state into the target repo.

Do not treat exit code 0 as a pass label. Status is only `running` or `exited`. `exit_code` is a number or null.

Agent skill: [skills/runtag/SKILL.md](skills/runtag/SKILL.md). Installed package: `node_modules/runtag/skills/runtag/SKILL.md` (this file at `node_modules/runtag/llms.txt`).

Once published: `npm i -g runtag` or `npx runtag`. From a checkout: `npm install`, then `node dist/cli.js`. Releasing: the first publish is a short-lived token bootstrap; later `v*` tags use OIDC in `publish.yml`. No long-lived `NPM_TOKEN`. See [docs/releasing.md](docs/releasing.md).

## Flow
1. `runtag exec --detach --cwd <repo> -- npm test`
   Read stdout JSON. Keep `id`.
2. `spacequery watch runs-in-dir --root <repo> --until status=exited`
   [spacequery](https://github.com/meganemura/spacequery) reads the job file and watches. runtag only records. An orphan stays `running` with `orphan: true` and `exit_code` null, and does not satisfy `status=exited`.
3. `runtag status <id>`
   Read `exit_code`.

## Commands
- `runtag exec [--cwd DIR] [--label NAME] [--detach] -- <cmd>...`
  No shell. The command belongs after `--`.
  Foreground: stdio is the child's; this process exits with the child code. State is still updated.
  `--detach`: stdout is the job JSON (`id`, `pid`, `status`); exit 0. A per-job supervisor keeps waiting and writes `exit_code`.
- `runtag status <id>` — one job JSON object on stdout.
- `runtag list [--root DIR] [--status running|exited]` — JSON array, newest `started_at` first. `--root` keeps jobs whose `repo_root` or `cwd` equals DIR or is inside DIR.
- `runtag gc [--older-than DURATION]` — delete exited jobs only. Default duration is `0s` (every exited job). Units: `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`.
- `runtag --help`

## State
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/runtag/jobs/<id>.json` (default `~/.local/share/runtag/jobs/`). Id is a ULID.

## Failures
Actionable failures print `{ "error", "do" }` on stderr and exit 1, or 127 if the executable could not be started (126 if it is not executable). Do what `do` says. A child exit code is not a failure envelope.

## Orphans
If the file says `running` and the supervisor pid is dead, the supervisor did not record an exit. `status` and `list` keep `status` `running` and `exit_code` null, and add `"orphan": true`. The file is not rewritten. Do not invent an exit code. Do not wait for `status=exited` on that id.

## Detach IO
Detached commands do not inherit the terminal. v0 discards their stdout and stderr. Run without `--detach` when you need the output.
